title: Proper subschemes of solvable homogeneous quotients have dimension zero
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $G$ is solvable, meaning that the iterated scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups eventually equal the trivial subgroup. Let $K\subseteq G$ be any closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], with no smoothness or connectedness assumption on $K$. Let $Q$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $q:G\to Q$ a faithfully flat morphism (flat and surjective), invariant under right multiplication by $K$, for which
$$G\times_k K\longrightarrow G\times_QG,\qquad (g,b)\longmapsto(g,gb)$$
is an isomorphism of schemes. Morphism properties and fibre products are as in [def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus these are explicit quotient data for $G/K$. Every nonempty closed $k$-subscheme $Z\subseteq Q$ that is proper over $k$ has topological Krull dimension $0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. In particular, if $Q$ itself is proper over $k$, then $K=G$ as closed subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 17.1, printed p.352 (PDF page 364), including its final assertion H=G when G/H is complete; quotient data as in Propositions 5.24--5.25 and 7.11, printed pp.104--105 and 141--142. No smoothness assumption on the subgroup.

proof.text: First identify the given $Q$ with the canonical $G/K$. Both maps out of $G$ are quasi-compact: apply finite-type cancellation to their separated finite-type targets over $k$. On the fpqc cover $G\to Q$, the canonical map $G\to G/K$ has equal pullbacks to $G\times_QG=G\times K$, by its right-$K$ invariance, hence descends uniquely to $Q\to G/K$. In the other direction descend $q$ along $G\to G/K$, using its kernel pair $G\times K$. The composites become identities after these covers, hence are identities by uniqueness of descent. These isomorphisms respect the quotient maps. Base change preserves this fpqc cover, so the same descent applies over $G\times(G/K)$. Left multiplication defines the action on $G/K$: locally $a\cdot(gK)=(ag)K$, and changing $g$ to $gb$ changes $ag$ to $agb$, so the local maps glue. The same formula verifies the action identities and the stabilizer at $eK$ is precisely $K$, on every test scheme.

source.place: Propositions 5.21, 5.24--5.25 and 7.11, printed pp.104--105, 141--142; fpqc gluing: Stacks descent.tex Tag 023Q

proof.text: The orbit-quotient statement identifies the reduced orbit of $eK$ with $G/K$, since its scheme-theoretic stabilizer is $K$. Combined with Step 1 this identifies $Q$ with that reduced orbit. The smooth-orbit statement therefore makes $Q$ smooth and reduced; the identity-component statement makes $G$ irreducible, so its surjective image $Q$ is irreducible and nonempty. Thus $Q$ is integral. We will prove the first assertion by strong induction on the nonnegative integer $d=\dim G$, simultaneously for every smooth connected solvable affine group of that dimension and every closed subgroup, including nonreduced or disconnected ones. The group-dimension statement supplies finiteness and nonnegativity. For $d=0$, $G$ is integral by the identity-component statement, hence is $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by the zero-dimensional integral-point theorem. Its only subgroup is itself: a closed subgroup has coordinate ring $k/I$ and its identity section forces $I=0$. Its quotient is a point, so every nonempty closed subscheme of the quotient has dimension zero.

source.place: Theorem 17.1, induction setup, printed p.352; group identity component: Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 0B7R; zero dimension: varieties.tex Tag 06LH

proof.text: Fix $d>0$ and assume the assertion already proved in every smaller group dimension, for arbitrary closed subgroups. Put $H=(K^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The nested-quotient lemma gives a smooth connected $H$ and a finite faithfully flat surjection $v:G/H\to G/K$. If $Z\subseteq G/K$ is nonempty closed and proper, then $W=Z\times_{G/K}(G/H)$ is closed in $G/H$ by closed-immersion base change. The map $W\to Z$ is finite and surjective, being the base change of the finite surjective $v$ (surjectivity is stable under base change), so $W$ is proper and nonempty and $\dim W=\dim Z$. Here properness follows from the finite-morphism permanence statement, and equality of dimensions from the finite-surjective dimension statement. It is enough to show $\dim W=0$, with the same $G$ and with the now smooth connected subgroup $H$.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 opening reduction, supplemented by Remark 7.16(b), printed pp.352, 143; Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 01WL and 01JY, algebra.tex Tag 00OK

proof.text: Replace $W$ by $W_{\mathrm{red}}$. The reduction is a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism, so dimension is unchanged and properness follows from closed-immersion properness. The proper reduced global-functions statement gives finitely many open and closed connected components $C$ of $W_{\mathrm{red}}$ and identifies their constant sections with $k$. Each such $C$ is reduced, nonempty, closed in $G/H$, and proper, with $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)=k$. It suffices to show $\dim C=0$ for every component: an irreducible subset of a finite disjoint open-and-closed union lies in one member, so every chain counted by dimension lies in a single component. No scheme-theoretic factorization of a nonreduced $W$ through a point is being asserted.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 reduction to connected Z, printed p.352; Stacks varieties.tex Tag 0BUG, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections (1)--(3), and morphisms.tex Tag 054M

proof.text: Let $D=D_G$. The derived-subgroup statement supplies a smooth connected affine normal closed subgroup of finite type. It is proper: write the solvable normal series as $G=G_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq G_m=1$ with commutative successive quotients. Inductively the $i$th derived subgroup lies in $G_i$, since its commutators die in $G_i/G_{i+1}$. Thus the derived series terminates. If $D=G$, every iterate instead equals $G$, forcing $G=1$, excluded by $d>0$. The strict dimension statement gives $\dim D<d$. Subgroups of $G$ that are smooth and connected are solvable: their successive derived subgroups lie in the corresponding derived subgroups of $G$, because restricting the commutator morphism preserves this containment, and the smallest-closed-subgroup property then preserves it at every iteration. They therefore become trivial when the derived series of $G$ does. This applies both to $D$ and to the smooth connected subgroup constructed next.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 derived subgroup, printed p.352; Corollary 6.19, Proposition 6.27 and Proposition 6.30, printed pp.129--132

proof.text: Construct the product without assuming $H$ normal. Form $a:G\to A=G/D$ by the affine normal-quotient statement. Factor $a|_H$ as the faithfully flat homomorphism $r:H\to I$ followed by a closed immersion $I\hookrightarrow A$. Its kernel is $L=D\cap H$, so $I$ represents $H/L$. The subgroup $L$ is normal in $H$, since $D$ is normal in $G$. Apply the affine normal-quotient statement to $H/L$: it is smooth and connected, since $H$ is smooth and geometrically connected (over the algebraically closed $k$, connectedness is already geometric in the specified algebraic-closure test). Put $N=G\times_A I$. The inverse-image clause of the same statement makes $N$ a smooth connected affine closed subgroup of finite type, since both $D$ and $I$ are smooth and connected. It contains $H$ and $D$. This uses the image factorization and the inverse-image clauses exactly, rather than invoking the normal-product lemma with a nonnormal $H$.

source.place: Section 5(f), product construction and Proposition 5.54, printed pp.111--112; Lemma 6.41, printed p.134

proof.text: Here $N=DH$ as fppf sheaves: a section $n$ of $N$ has $a(n)\in I$; lift it locally through $r$ to $h\in H$. Then $nh^{-1}\in D$, giving $n=dh$. Conversely $dh$ maps into $I$. The group $A=G/D$ is commutative: lift two of its sections locally to $g_1,g_2\in G$, whose commutator lies in $D$, and descend the resulting commutativity identity. Thus every subgroup $I$ of $A$ is normal, and the inverse-image normality clause makes $N$ normal in $G$. By the preceding derived-series containment, $N$ is solvable. If $N\ne G$, its dimension is strictly less than $d$ by the strict dimension statement.

source.place: Section 5(f), product description, printed p.111; Theorem 17.1 contrary case, printed p.352

proof.text: If $N=G$, the map $D/(D\cap H)\to G/H$, $d(D\cap H)\mapsto dH$, is an isomorphism of schemes. Indeed $G=DH$ gives local surjectivity on the quotient sheaves. Two sections $d,d'$ have the same image precisely when $d^{-1}d'\in H$; since both lie in $D$, this is precisely membership in $D\cap H$. These local bijections and their inverses are compatible with pullback and glue by the sheaf property. Both sheaves are represented by the stated homogeneous-quotient schemes, so the natural maps are inverse scheme morphisms. The closed proper $C\subseteq G/H$ becomes a closed proper subscheme of this quotient of $D$. The induction hypothesis for $D$, whose dimension is smaller, gives $\dim C=0$. The subgroup $D\cap H$ may be nonreduced or disconnected; the induction hypothesis was deliberately stated to allow this.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 case G=G′H, printed p.352; coset argument of Theorem 5.52, printed p.112

proof.text: Suppose $N\ne G$. It is normal, so form the affine quotient $B=G/N$ using the affine normal-quotient statement. Apply the nested-quotient statement to $H\subseteq N\subseteq G$ to obtain $b:G/H\to G/N$. Restrict it to $C$. Since $B$ is affine and $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)=k$, the morphism-into-affine-scheme bijection says that $b|_C$ factors as $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k\xrightarrow{y}B$, with $y$ the $k$-point defined by the map on global sections. The homogeneous-quotient rational-lift clause supplies $g\in G(k)$ mapping to $y$. The translated-fibre clause of the nested-quotient statement identifies the scheme fibre $b^{-1}(y)$ with $N/H$ by $nH\mapsto gnH$. The universal property of the fibre product therefore gives a factorization $C\to b^{-1}(y)$. This is a closed immersion: its pullback description is $C\times_{G/H}b^{-1}(y)=C$, and closed immersions are stable under base change.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 affine quotient and fibre step, printed p.352; Proposition 7.15 Cartesian square and Remark 7.16(a), printed pp.142--143; affine morphism bijection: Stacks schemes.tex Tag 01I1

proof.text: We now have $C$ as a closed subscheme of $N/H$, proper over $k$. The ambient group $N$ is smooth, connected, affine, solvable and of finite type by Steps 6--7, and $\dim N<d$. Thus the induction hypothesis applied to $N$ and its closed subgroup $H$ gives $\dim C=0$. Together with Step 8 this handles every component of $W_{\mathrm{red}}$; Step 4 gives $\dim W=0$, and Step 3 gives $\dim Z=0$. This completes the strong induction for the first assertion. The alternatives $D=1$, $H=1$, and $H=G$ are included: no positive dimension or smoothness of an intersection was assumed.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 final induction step, printed p.352

proof.text: Finally suppose $Q$ is proper. It is nonempty because $q$ is surjective and $G$ has its identity point. The proved assertion applied to $Z=Q$ gives $\dim Q=0$. Step 2 showed that this original $Q$, with the original arbitrary $K$, is integral; the zero-dimensional integral-point theorem therefore gives $Q\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its quotient point $q(e)$ is consequently the entire scheme $Q$. Pull back the specified isomorphism $G\times K\simeq G\times_QG$ along $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ in the first coordinate. The result identifies the given inclusion $K\hookrightarrow G$ with the fibre $q^{-1}(q(e))\hookrightarrow G$. Since $q(e)$ is all of $Q$, that fibre inclusion is the identity of $G$. Hence $K=G$ as closed subgroup schemes, including their infinitesimal structure.

source.place: Theorem 17.1 final assertion, printed p.352; Proposition 5.24 kernel-pair identity, printed p.104

Item: the statement is unchanged from the base, and the item is still unsplit live, so nothing supersedes it. There is no repair note, so this is a first split. Theorem 17.1 (printed p.352): the 11 steps follow Milne's route. That route is induction on dim G with the derived group D: if DH=G then G/H≅D/(D∩H); otherwise N=DH is normal, G/N is affine, each component C maps to a point and lies in a fibre ≅N/H. Milne's proof has a real gap: it makes H only smooth, then calls N=G'H connected (6.41). This fails for disconnected H: with G=G_m and H=μ_n, G'=1 and N=μ_n is disconnected. The worker's repair is correct: replace K by H=(K^0)_red, using the finite faithfully flat map G/H→G/K from 7.16(b). Step checks: step 1 identifies Q with G/K by descent along fpqc covers and computes the stabilizer as K. Step 2 gets Q integral from the reduced-orbit and smooth-orbit clauses, states the strong induction explicitly, and handles the base case with zero-dim-integral-point. In step 4 the proper reduced global-sections node applies only after reduction, which gives Γ(C)=k. Step 6 builds N=G×_{G/D}I through the image factorization and the inverse-image clause, so it never needs H normal. Step 7 gets A commutative, so N is normal. Step 9 uses Hom into affine schemes, the rational lift and the translated-fibre clause, and C→b^{-1}(y) is a closed immersion. Step 11 pulls back the kernel pair to get K=G as schemes. Every cited clause says what its step uses. New node lem-sfb-nested-homogeneous-quotient-geometry: it is true. After pulling back along q_J, π becomes G×(J/H)→G, and when dim J/H=0 the fibre J/H is finite. This matches Milne 7.15 (square)/7.16(b); the second sentence of 7.15 prints the arrow reversed, as the worker reported. I tested H=J, μ_p⊂J, J=G and μ_2⊂G_m. The node meets B1–B7 and does not restate the item. lean.statement: theorem solvable_homogeneous_proper_subschemes {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G K : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj K] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [IsAffine G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (hsolv : IsSolvableGroupScheme G) (i : K ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] (Q : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsSeparated Q.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Q.hom] [QuasiCompact Q.hom] (q : G ⟶ Q) [Flat q.left] [Surjective q.left] (hinv : fst G K ≫ q = lift (fst G K) (snd G K ≫ i) ≫ μ[G] ≫ q) (e : G ⊗ K ≅ pullback q q) (he₁ : e.hom ≫ pullback.fst q q = fst G K) (he₂ : e.hom ≫ pullback.snd q q = lift (fst G K) (snd G K ≫ i) ≫ μ[G]) : (∀ (Z : Over (Spec (.of k))) (j : Z ⟶ Q), IsClosedImmersion j.left → Nonempty Z.left → IsProper Z.hom → topologicalKrullDim Z.left = 0) ∧ (IsProper Q.hom → IsIso i)
lean.note: Uses the landed scheme-theoretic derived-series definition from def-sfb-semisimple-group-scheme. The two projection identities specify the canonical kernel-pair isomorphism. IsIso i expresses K = G as closed subgroup schemes, including nonreduced structure.
